clue.text: Tea boy with yen for older female worker?

parts.note: char is British slang for a cup of tea
a lad is a boy
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: An office tea boy has been swapped for an older woman because someone fancied her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea boy' reads as one job title, but it splits into two pieces. A CHAR or charlady is a British cleaning woman, an old-fashioned word, which is why the definition says 'older'.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlady is a woman paid to clean houses or offices, a job and word from an earlier era.

clue.text: Firm animated having collected right group of people

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: having collected means holding something gathered inside

parts.note: hot can mean excited or animated

explanation.surface: A lively company has gathered the correct team together.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohort is a band of people grouped together, originally a Roman military unit.

clue.text: An unpleasant task for a villain

explanation.surface: A dirty job set for a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a nasty person, and literally a disagreeable piece of labour.

clue.text: Scot of some means in den with daughter

parts.note: a lair is an animal's den

explanation.surface: A wealthy Scotsman relaxes in his den with his daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish landowner, typically a man of property and wealth.

clue.text: One got rid of blemish, managed to hide it

indicators.note: to hide means something is concealed inside the other piece

parts.note: did means managed, as in 'did well'
a scar is a mark or blemish on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone who removed a flaw tried to cover it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One got rid of' is a noun phrase: the thing thrown away, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A discard is an item rejected or thrown away, as in a card game.

clue.text: Words of reluctant acceptance not good enough

definitions.meaning: a shrugging phrase said when one gives in to something unwelcome
a verdict that something falls below the standard needed

explanation.surface: Someone grudgingly accepts a result that is still unsatisfactory.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a resigned shrug ('pity, but there it is') and a literal judgment of excess badness.

clue.text: In every respect unfashionable, aunt moved around party

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion

indicators.note: around says the shuffled letters go round the party word
moved signals the letters of aunt are shifted about

parts.note: a do is a party or social event

explanation.surface: An out-of-date aunt circulates at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' scrambles aunt to ANUT, which is split by the party word.
explanation.definitionFit: Out-and-out means complete and thorough, absolute in every way.

clue.text: Hefty drunk with no breeding in satirical show

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A burly drunk with no manners turns up in a comedy revue.
explanation.walkthrough: BEYOND THE FRINGE was a 1960s British satirical revue starring Peter Cook and Dudley Moore.
explanation.definitionFit: The revue launched the British satire boom of the early 1960s.

clue.text: Ridiculous order is changed before end of day

indicators.note: changed signals that the letters of order is are rearranged
end of picks the final letter of day

explanation.surface: An absurd instruction gets altered before the day ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' reads as part of 'is changed', but it belongs to the fodder: ORDERIS rearranged makes DERISOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Derisory means so small or inadequate as to be laughable.

clue.text: Fades in preliminary race that's most exciting

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece sits inside the race word

parts.note: a heat is a qualifying race before the final
dies, as a sound or light dies away, means fades

explanation.surface: A runner flags midway through a qualifying heat, which made it the most thrilling race.
explanation.definitionFit: Heady means intoxicating or exhilarating, so the superlative is the most thrilling.

clue.text: Saint and philosopher who won't give up?

parts.note: A. J. Ayer was a British philosopher of logical positivism

explanation.surface: A saint and a philosopher are praised for their persistence.
explanation.definitionFit: A stayer is a horse or person with stamina who keeps going to the finish.

clue.text: Uriah is an unthinking follower heading off

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter of the follower word

parts.note: a sheep is someone who follows the crowd mindlessly

explanation.surface: Uriah is a mindless follower who wanders off.
explanation.definitionFit: Uriah Heep is the obsequious villain of Dickens's David Copperfield.

clue.text: Admired artist, rebel of the fifties

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist
a Ted or Teddy boy was a rebellious British youth of the 1950s with drape jackets

explanation.surface: A painter who was a young rebel in the fifties was much admired.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were a 1950s British youth subculture, dressed in Edwardian-style suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Something highly rated is well regarded, so rated serves as admired.

clue.text: A writer's traversing square in the mountains

indicators.note: traversing means crossing through, so the number goes across the middle of the writer's piece

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument, and the possessive 's adds an S
nine is a square number, three times three

explanation.surface: A pen-pusher crosses a town square while holidaying in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' looks like a place, but it means a square number, as nine is three times three.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apennines are the mountain range running down the length of Italy.

clue.text: Humbled, like journalist encountering a bishop

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
as means like, in the sense of similar to
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is put in his place after meeting a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abased is to be lowered in dignity, made humble.

clue.text: Quality of cliffs in Kent location

definitions.meaning: the steep, near-vertical character of a cliff face
a port town on the Isle of Sheppey in Kent, south-east England

explanation.surface: The steepness of cliffs at a place in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer cliffs are vertical; the noun also names a town in the county of Kent.

clue.text: Schemer to amble outside back of hall

indicators.note: outside says the strolling word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to potter is to move about in a leisurely, unhurried way

indicators.note: back of points to the final letter of hall

explanation.surface: A conspirator wanders about just outside the rear of a hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A plotter is someone who devises secret plans, a conspirator.

clue.text: This person's given support with little hesitation — it's wrong

parts.note: this person is I, so this person's is I'm
a prop is a support
er is a brief hesitation sound

explanation.surface: Someone propped up who hesitates slightly is in the wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper means unsuitable or incorrect, not right.

clue.text: Affairs make a difference — the end of faithfulness

parts.note: to matter is to be important, to make a difference

indicators.note: the end of signals the last letter of faithfulness

explanation.surface: Extramarital affairs really count when they finish off fidelity.
explanation.definitionFit: Matters are affairs in the sense of business or concerns, as in 'personal matters'.

clue.text: Snow now melting and child makes dangerous move

indicators.note: melting means the word disappears from the snow

parts.note: a kid is a child

explanation.surface: As snow thaws, a child takes a risky slide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snow now melting' takes NOW out of SNOW, leaving S.
explanation.definitionFit: A skid is a sliding loss of control, a hazardous movement.

clue.text: Grumble coming from maiden given voice

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
to utter is to give voice to something

explanation.surface: A young woman voices her complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutter is to complain in low, indistinct tones, a synonym for grumble.

clue.text: Not a stone to raise — big weight

indicators.note: to raise, in a down entry, means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: Something this heavy is not a mere stone you could lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stone' looks like a unit of weight, but it is a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: A megaton is a million tons, a vast weight.

clue.text: Moved quickly with trousers unlikely to fall down?

definitions.meaning: to belt is to rush along at speed

definitions.text: with trousers unlikely to fall down?
definitions.meaning: wearing a belt to hold up one's trousers

explanation.surface: Someone dashed off with their trousers held securely.
explanation.definitionFit: Belted means raced along, and also wearing a belt around the waist.

clue.text: It could be grim for one losing love, making a new start

indicators.note: could be says the letters may be rearranged into something else

parts.note: taken as written, the letter pool
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Starting over could be grim for someone who has lost a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Take GRIMFORONE, remove one O ('losing love'), and rearrange the rest to get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Reforming means changing one's ways for the better, turning over a new leaf.

clue.text: Agency supporting the established church

parts.note: for means in favour of, supporting
CE is the Church of England, England's established church

explanation.surface: An agency backs the state church.
explanation.definitionFit: Agency here is power to act or cause effects, which a force is.

clue.text: Ships going full steam ahead?

explanation.surface: A navy of steamers presses on at top speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet is a group of ships and, as an adjective, swift.

clue.text: Call by made by unknown character — one attempting a scam?

parts.note: to phone is to call by telephone
Y is one of the letters used for unknown quantities in algebra

explanation.surface: A scam caller dials from an anonymous number.
explanation.definitionFit: A phoney is a fraud or impostor, someone trying to pass themselves off falsely.

clue.text: Enter the new computer system

indicators.note: new means remade, so the two words are formed afresh in a different order

explanation.surface: An instruction to log on to a fresh computer network.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethernet is the standard wired networking technology connecting computers in a local network.

clue.text: Jaunty queen and king half hidden in wood

parts.note: R is short for Regina, queen

indicators.note: hidden in says one piece is tucked inside the tree word

parts.note: ash is a tree and its timber

indicators.note: half takes the first two of the four letters of king

explanation.surface: A cheerful queen and king are half concealed in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half hidden' reads as one phrase, but 'half' acts on king alone, giving its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rakish means dashingly carefree, often of a hat worn at a jaunty angle.

clue.text: Edge of bank by river containing no troublesome plant

indicators.note: containing says the first pieces hold the next one between them
edge of picks out the final letter of bank

parts.note: the Tweed is a river forming part of the England-Scotland border

explanation.surface: A riverbank where no weeds are allowed to spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese knotweed is an invasive plant notorious for damaging buildings and gardens.
